audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart read Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Skill/Skill/Skill/Ryze; the content layer and the packet chart both read Hwei on all seven rows. Four rows disagreed across layers.
audit.why: Ryze has no dash and both Spell Flux and Rune Prison stop at 615, while Hwei paints from well outside that. Nothing in his kit changes that at 4-5, 6 or first item — Realm Warp is a rotation tool at 3000 range, not a lane spike.
audit.corrected: Rows 4-5, level 6, first item and 2+ items moved to Hwei to match the packet and content layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 and item spikes were described without a single Ryze number, and Arcane Mastery was called a 'stacking passive'.
audit.why: Arcane Mastery scales his spell damage off bonus MANA and converts AP into max mana — it does not stack in combat. Realm Warp is 180/160/140 at 3000 range. Overload's real spike is the reset pattern: it is 5s base but every other ability cast resets it.
audit.corrected: spikes[1]-[3] and breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with the real mechanic and numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page treats Rune Prison as a root. It is a slow — it only roots if Spell Flux is already on the target. The content layer also said the root needs 'Overload (Q) stacks on you', which is the wrong ability entirely.
audit.why: Riot's W text: traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging and slowing them; if the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted. Flux comes from Spell Flux (E), 615 range, 3.5s falling to 2.5s. That makes the counterplay concrete: break the E-then-W order and there is no root at all.
audit.corrected: Stated in winCon, enemyWin, tradeBad, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it, and 'Punish his short dash range' credits Ryze with a dash he does not have.
audit.why: Ryze's kit contains no dash flag and no mobility ability. His only repositioning is Realm Warp's portal.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written in; the dash reference replaced with the walk-up to 615.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two COPY_PASTE_BLEED bullets, and early claims you will have 'chunked him for 40% HP' before the root lands.
audit.why: The 40% is a magnitude with no source in either kit.
audit.corrected: Bled bullets rewritten to match their titles; the invented percentage removed.

edits.before: Ryze is one of the safest lane matchups you'll play — he has almost no way to punish your poke range at levels 1-5. His only engage is a root that requires him to walk into your Q/E zone first, and you'll have already chunked him for 40% HP before that root lands. Just don't stand still in his root range past level 3 when his passive starts giving him extra damage, and keep shoving to deny his stacking pattern.

His prison only roots through Spell Flux, and Flux stops at 615, so he has to walk into your zone before anything starts. Just don't stand still inside 615 once he has E, and keep shoving so he never farms the mana his passive turns into damage.

notes:
Chart: full layer read Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Skill/Skill/Skill/Ryze; content win[N] and packet.levelChart both read Hwei on all seven rows at a 56% win rate over 1809 games. I moved the four disagreeing full-layer sides to Hwei. No paired win[N] edits are included because win[N] is already correct on disk.

Biggest factual fix: the page treats Rune Prison as a root. It is a slow unless Spell Flux is already applied. That single conditional is the counterplay in this lane and it was nowhere on the page.

Also corrected: Ryze credited with a dash he does not have; Arcane Mastery called a 'stacking passive' (it scales off bonus mana); and the content layer said the root needs 'Overload stacks'.
